transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-26
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Alex Park (CTO - Helix), Sam Ortiz (Infra Lead - Helix), Mina Shah (SecOps - Helix), Jorge Alvarez (ML Eng - Helix)

Auto-generated summary: Weekly checkin for Redwood Private (VPC) pilot. Focus on networking, perf, and upgrade window.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Alex (Helix): Alex here.
[00:09] Sam (Helix): Sam here.
[00:11] Mina (Helix): Mina here.
[00:13] Jorge (Helix): Jorge here.
[00:15] Diego (Redwood): Diego here. Good to see you all.

[00:20] Maya: Great — quick agenda, diego will walk the perf results, then Sam we want to go over the peering traceroute you sent, then security Qs and upgrade plan. Any additions?
[00:28] Alex: No, that's good. We're particularly keen on that p95 number — it's what our product folks look at.

[00:35] Diego: Okay I'll share my screen — I uploaded the run results to the shared drive in case anyone wants to follow along. Note these are the 2-node private pilot results, mixed traffic: some short prompts and a few 8k context long prompts.
[00:48] Diego: Observed metrics: p50 ~ 120 ms on small prompts (token generation only), p95 ~ 480 ms on mixed workload, and long-context 8k runs hit p95 ~ 1.1s. Throughput with concurrency 8 was about 28 rps sustained. We saw token-level costs roughly equivalent to our hosted profile assuming quantized 4-bit model.
[01:15] Jorge: Couple of clarifying q's — those p95 numbers, are they end-to-end (including network/ingress) or purely host-side?
[01:22] Diego: Good call — they're end-to-end from the test harness running inside Helix VPC to the model. So they include the VPC networking latency. Host-side alone was ~80% of that for the long runs. So network is contributing but not the only factor.

[01:40] Sam: Right — on the traceroutes I ran, we saw an occasional MTU drop where packets hit a 1360 boundary and get fragmented. That lines up with spikes. I put the tcpdump in the share.
[01:50] Diego: That explains lots of the p95 spikes — fragmentation causes extra retransmits and stalls the KV cache warmup.

[02:05] Mina: Also want to note our Sec team saw a gap in the audit log retention sample — the initial deploy retained only 7 days not 90 as our policy states. Is that configurable?
[02:15] Maya: Yes — the platform supports configurable retention for audit logs in the private control plane; Diego, can you confirm the config path?
[02:22] Diego: Yeah it's a controller flag in the helm chart — audit.logRetentionDays. In private we can surface that through the operator values.yaml. We should set it to 90 and tie it to your S3/KMS bucket.

[02:35] Mina: And KMS — we need to ensure we can bring our key, HSM-backed if possible. We previously sent the KMS integration doc.
[02:44] Maya: We support customer-managed keys for the private control plane; HSM integration is available but requires the enterprise package. I'll add that to the follow-up pricing note.

[02:58] Alex: On the upgrade window — you mentioned a driver/kernel bump. What downtime should we expect?
[03:05] Diego: So the proposed plan is staggered reboot of inference nodes. For a rolling kernel/driver upgrade, we'd recommend a 2-hour window for the entire cluster to allow CNI restarts and health checks; actual per-node disruption is small but there's an operator coord step. If you want zero impact we can fallback to hosted during the window but that adds cost.
[03:25] Sam: Two hours is acceptable if it's off-peak, but we need detailed steps and a rollback plan. Also want to verify NCCL and CUDA versions — we're on CUDA 12.2 and a relatively new driver.
[03:35] Diego: We're testing on CUDA 12.2 driver 535+ in staging; the new kernels improve attention kernel scheduling and reduce p95 by ~10-15% in our internal benchmarks.

[03:50] Jorge: Quick question about fallback: If during the upgrade the private cluster becomes unavailable, how seamless is fallback to hosted? Do we lose KV cache and prefix caching benefits?
[03:59] Maya: Fallback policy is model-aware. You will get a different model endpoint in hosted; KV cache won't be shared across private->hosted, so some cold-start latency will happen. Diego, add the exact behavior to the follow-up doc.
[04:12] Diego: Will do. Also capture the suggested routing policy: prefer private, failover to dedicated hosted pool in same region with warm cache pre-warm options.

[04:25] Alex: Back to the network — Sam, you mentioned fragmentation. Can you explain what changed last week that might have caused it?
[04:32] Sam: We did a VPC peering change to route through a transit gateway; default MTU on the gateway is 1360, so jumbo frames get truncated. We can bump the path MTU or move to direct VPC peering without transit for the inference subnet. Diego suggested checking for DF (don't fragment) bit behavior.
[04:48] Diego: If you can remove the transit hop for the inference path, p95 should drop significantly. Alternatively, we can use HTTP/2 chunking to reduce large packets, but that's more of an app workaround.

[05:05] Mina: From a security perspective, transit gateway throws us some concerns around logging and egress control — we prefer direct peering for the inference path.
[05:13] Maya: Noted. We'll mark that as recommended configuration.

[05:20] Alex: Regarding cost, Maya, can you share a ballpark node sizing and monthly estimate for the pilot if we move to dedicated reserved nodes? We're evaluating economics vs hosted fallback.
[05:30] Maya: Sure — based on your current load, for production you'd likely need 3 dedicated A100-class nodes (or their equivalent optimized configs) to reach your SLOs with headroom; monthly committed pricing estimate I will send but rough ballpark is $XXk/month for the reserved pool plus support. I'll include quantization and batching tuning to reduce apparent cost.
[05:50] Jorge: Can the runtime do continuous batching with our traffic shape or will we need to rework our request patterns?
[05:58] Diego: The runtime does continuous batching and KV prefix caching; you'll get better amortization when you have burstiness. We also recommended a small client-side retry/backoff to allow micro-batching windows. I can share sample client libs that implement the pattern.

[06:15] Alex: Good — about the SOC 2 questions, Mina will follow-up but anything Redwood needs to provide?
[06:21] Maya: We'll share the SOC 2 summary, your private deployment will have separate audit logs and we'll include KMS integration notes. Also, Diego will add the retention and access control docs.

[06:35] Diego: Quick note on model upgrades — the pilot is currently on open-model v2.1 quantized. Upgrading to 2.2 reduces latency for long-context by ~8%, but we need to validate output quality on your eval set. Jorge, do you want us to run a diff on the eval prompts you provided?
[06:50] Jorge: Yes please — run the model diff and flag any regressions. We'll share the eval bundle in the drive.

[06:58] Mina: Also confirm data at rest encryption with customer-managed keys and rotation policy, and whether logs are exported to our SIEM.
[07:07] Diego: Encryption at rest uses your KMS key for S3 buckets and the control plane secrets; rotation is supported via standard KMS rotation. Audit exports to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export — we'll document wiring.

[07:22] Sam: One more infra note — ingress LB idle timeout was default 60s; for long contexts that times out and causes client disconnects. We bumped to 300s in the test cluster and that solved some of the long-run failures.
[07:33] Diego: Good catch — we'll add that to the recommended helm values (service.beta.aws/elb-idle-timeout: 300).

[07:42] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll send the pricing + node recommendation. Diego will share the optimized helm values, fallback behavior doc, and add the model-diff plan. Sam to confirm MTU/peering telemetry. Jorge to run the 10k token run. Mina to confirm SOC2/KMS follow-ups.

[07:58] Alex: That works. Also propose a tentative upgrade window week of 2027-09-06; we'll confirm by next Tuesday.
[08:06] Maya: Perfect — we'll pencil that in and propose a specific two-hour window in the follow-up.

[08:12] Jorge: One quick nit — the perf logs show a line with "gpu-oom" on run #42 but the memory graphs looked fine; might be a transient fragmentation event. I'll attach the logs and timestamp.
[08:22] Diego: We'll correlate with driver logs; if it's transient we'll add a retry guard in the runner.

[08:30] Mina: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:33] Maya: Only open items are getting the final SOC2 snippet and KMS pricing. Diego will deliver the config notes. We'll follow up in Slack thread.

[08:41] Alex: Thanks everyone.
[08:43] Maya: Thanks all — talk soon.
